paragraphs: The hardware platform selected for this implementation is the popular STM32F103C8T6 development board, widely designated as the 'Blue Pill'. The board incorporates an STM32F103C8T6 microcontroller featuring an ARM Cortex-M3 32-bit RISC core operating at a maximum clock frequency of 72 MHz. The device integrates 64 KB of embedded Flash memory for program code storage and 20 KB of high-speed SRAM for data allocation.

The board is powered by an onboard 3.3V low-dropout voltage regulator capable of accepting 5V input via USB or an external power supply. An external 8 MHz quartz crystal oscillator serves as the high-speed external (HSE) clock source, which is multiplied by the internal phase-locked loop (PLL) to deliver the system core clock of 72 MHz. An auxiliary 32.768 kHz crystal supports the integrated real-time clock (RTC).
